clue.text: Female worker, unnamed Asian, in Disney film

indicators.note: without a name means losing the letter that stands for name, so one letter drops away

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker
taken as written, before the N for name is removed

explanation.surface: A woman labourer of Asian origin, never named, appears in a Disney cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the usual abbreviation for name, so unnamed takes the N off ASIAN. FANTASIA is the 1940 Disney film set to classical music.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the title of Disney's 1940 animated feature, so it is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Take it back to monarch at one level

indicators.note: taking something back returns it the opposite way, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: An instruction to return something to the king or queen while standing on one floor.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the cipher of Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one row or layer in a stacked arrangement, a synonym for a level.

clue.text: Have silly nerd in for a meal

indicators.note: something silly is foolish and disordered, so the letters lose their sensible order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Invite a foolish geek round for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, a specific kind of meal.

clue.text: Composer — that's him speaking back in way

indicators.note: speaking means we hear the word rather than see it, so a word that sounds the same is wanted

blocks.note: a word pronounced just like him
the initial of in
St, street, is a common abbreviation for a way or road

explanation.surface: Pointing someone out as a composer, voice heard from the back of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is loose: the sound of the pronoun gives the opening clearly, but 'back' seems to be padding, with the initial of 'in' placed before the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymnist writes hymns, so is a composer of a particular kind of sacred song.

clue.text: Rudolph could be thus described

blocks.note: surface reading: a description of a person called Rudolph
setter's reading: Rudolph the red-nosed reindeer, and what grows on his head

explanation.walkthrough: Rudolph seems to be any man so named; it is the reindeer, whose head carries branched horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer of both sexes grow branched horns, so Rudolph has them and is described by the adjective.

clue.text: Lid cleaner changed in a child's tale

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters do not stay as they are but are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pot lid gets swapped for a cleaning one in a story for children.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Cinderella spends her days cleaning before the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is the famous fairy story of the glass slipper, an example of a children's tale.

clue.text: 25 gains first point in a Rugby game

blocks.note: a compass point, placed first
the answer to 25 across

explanation.surface: Clue 25 picks up the opening score in a rugby match.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 25 across is EVENS; S, south, is a point of the compass placed in front. Sevens is rugby played with seven a side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side form of rugby union, played as a short fast match.

clue.text: It's consumed by outrageous vanity from birth

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so these letters sit inside the others
outrageous suggests something wild and out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something has been swallowed up by monstrous conceit from the day one was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Nativity means the circumstances of a person's birth, a formal synonym.

clue.text: One concealed in part of church is innocent

indicators.note: something concealed in a place is kept inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: the nave is the main body of a church
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person hidden in a section of a church building is guiltless.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means unworldly and lacking experience, close to innocent in its trusting sense.

clue.text: Big billing for one of the Gemini!

blocks.note: first meaning: top billing goes to the lead performer
second meaning: Castor and Pollux, the Twins, are bright celestial bodies

explanation.walkthrough: Gemini looks like a star sign or a horoscope; it is the constellation, whose two brightest points of light are Castor and Pollux.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading performer gets big billing, and each twin of the Gemini constellation is a shining sun in the night sky.

clue.text: A number of women cutting a caper in a Christmas song

definitions.note: a phrase from a song, not a song

blocks.note: a count of females: nine of them
to cut a caper is to leap about playfully

explanation.surface: A group of women frolicking in a festive carol.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the ninth day's gift in The Twelve Days of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twelve Days of Christmas lists nine ladies dancing among the gifts my true love sent, so the phrase is found in that carol.

clue.text: Line showing pressure is round at the pub

blocks.note: taken as written
a round shape like the letter O
a bar is a pub or drinking place

explanation.surface: It's my turn to buy drinks in the pub, under pressure to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Buck Mr Bean made from previous issue

indicators.note: made means formed or constructed, so the letters are built into something new

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stag, or a dollar, fashioned out of the comic character Mr Bean, an old edition.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Bean is Rowan Atkinson's bumbling TV character.
explanation.definitionFit: A back number is an earlier copy of a magazine or newspaper, the same as a past issue.

clue.text: Spur broken on an incline that''s unexpected

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: something unexpected

indicators.note: a thing broken is in pieces that can be put back in any order

blocks.note: taken as written
a rise is an upward slope

explanation.surface: A rider's spur snaps on a slope, which nobody saw coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise is an event or thing nobody expected, the noun matching the adjective.

clue.text: See 11
Rising school on trial opens wallet

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: Eton is the famous English public school
a court case is a trial

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming school under trial opens a billfold.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is the elite English boarding school, a crossword stalwart.
explanation.definitionFit: A notecase is an old word for a wallet for holding banknotes.

clue.text: Sadly, CID surround poor Lily in circumstances that are charming

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled
poor suggests something badly made, so these letters are also rearranged
to surround is to go all around, so one group of letters wraps the other

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Detectives unhappily close in on unfortunate Lily, in a setting that is otherwise delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Idyllic describes something peacefully pleasant like a pastoral scene, a near synonym of delightful.

clue.text: Become greater within the fold

blocks.note: within means in
a fold in paper or cloth is a crease

explanation.surface: Grow larger while staying inside the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Within the fold' looks like one phrase about sheep or belonging; split it into two words read one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase is to grow in size or number, the same verb sense as getting bigger.

clue.text: Possibly locate unknown attendant

indicators.note: possibly hints at one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: Perhaps find an anonymous helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant to a priest, or more broadly a follower, so an attendant.

clue.text: Free without new spasm but uncontrollable

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: No longer new and free, but racked by a spasm one can't control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without new' looks like taking a letter away; here without means outside, so FREE goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means wildly agitated and frantic, behaviour that is beyond restraint.

clue.text: One staggering dancer

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who lurches unsteadily
second meaning: someone who performs a Scottish reel

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an astonishing performer; the word means both a person who totters and one who dances reels.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is both to lurch drunkenly and to dance the lively Scottish reel, so one doing either fits.

clue.text: Change club for good; it's a gamble

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in, so a letter is exchanged

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for club in card games
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Swapping golf clubs for keeps is a risk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is a risk taken on an uncertain outcome, a synonym of a gamble.

clue.text: Cruises turn out in unstable periods

indicators.note: putting something out removes it, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a U-turn, so turn gives the letter U

explanation.surface: Pleasure voyages become times of upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn out' looks like 'prove to be'; it is a U-turn, the letter U, taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are times of acute difficulty or danger, when things are unsettled.

clue.text: Food for little worms in Italy

blocks.note: first meaning: a very thin pasta
second meaning: the literal Italian sense of the pasta's name

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like bait or bird food; the Italian name of the pasta literally means little worms.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermicelli is thin pasta whose Italian name translates as small worms.

clue.text: See 26
Fixing to take final awkward fellow out

indicators.note: to take something out is to remove it, so a letter goes
awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the remaining letters are shuffled about

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A repair job removes the last clumsy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail is a small metal spike used for fastening, so a fixing in the hardware sense.

clue.text: Bet some believe en suite is necessary

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so just part of the next word is kept
loosely, only what is necessary of the last word is kept, its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut to its last three letters
en is the spelt-out name of the letter N
just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A wager that some think a private bathroom is a must.
explanation.walkthrough: It looks like a run of letters straight through believe en suite, but that holds one E too many; en has to be read as the name of a letter. An en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens is a bet at odds of one to one, where the stake is matched by the winnings.

clue.text: Carol ruined fortieth lens

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so its letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's lens on their fortieth birthday is spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: The First Noel is a traditional English Christmas carol, an example of the category.
